\section{Purpose}

When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.

The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
lemma was applied.

The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
prose.

\section{Concision and Readability}

A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.

The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
derivation genuinely needs room.

Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.

If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
the issue or pull request in a footnote.

\section{When the Investigation Starts}

The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
argument.

The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
relevant files already compile.

At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
formalized.

A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
mathematics.

Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.

Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
implementation.

\section{When to Write a Note}

A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
relation.

A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.

Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.

When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
though it were the paper theorem.

This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
argument.

A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.

\section{Counterexamples}

If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.

When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.

\section{Revision of a Note}

A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
which point remains unsettled.

Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
discussion.

\section{Form of the Note}

Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
around the mathematical assertion and its proof.

The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.

Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.

Displayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the
source estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and
the calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a
displayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on
the right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical
assertion itself.  The standard \texttt{amsmath} command \verb|\tag| is the
right mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only
if the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned
display, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than
forcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short
scalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the
sentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed
formula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.

Bibliographic entries used only by these notes should live in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/references.bib}.  A new note should ordinarily begin from
\path{docs/paper-gaps/template.tex}, which records the common LaTeX preamble,
the local bibliography, and a model for right-hand source labels in displayed
equations.

Blueprint prose cites a note like any other source, with
\verb|\cite{gap:<slug>}|; the bibliography entry in
\path{blueprint/src/references.bib} carries the published URL of the note,
whether the note lives in this repository or in another one.  Lean docstrings
and comments use the repository path form \path{docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex}.

The note should then compare the cited source with the informal blueprint, if
there is one, and with the formal statement.  This comparison should be written
in ordinary mathematical prose.  Formal declaration names and source paths should
be supplied only to identify the exact formal statements, and normally belong in
footnotes.

The conclusion should give a verdict.  It may say that there is no discrepancy,
that the matter is only notational, that an intermediate estimate needs a
harmless correction, that a hypothesis is missing, that there is a theorem-level
gap, or that the question remains open.  The classification should reflect the
mathematics, not the amount of formal work required.

\section{Decision Principle}

The formal development should not silently replace the cited assertion by a
different one.  If the formal statement differs from the cited source, the
reason for the difference should be written down.  Conversely, the note should
not overstate the conclusion.  A wrong intermediate scalar is not a fatal gap in
the theorem if the corrected scalar is bounded by the error parameter appearing
in the theorem statement.

\author{}
\date{2026-05-11}

\section{Purpose}

This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
A proof may be blocked at
an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
theorem
may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.

The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.

\section{Basic objects}

\paragraph{Source theorem.}
A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
documented paper-gap corrections.

\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
not assume.

\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.

\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.

\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
content; it does not close the source theorem.

\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}

The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Bridge.}
A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.

\paragraph{Residual.}
A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.

\paragraph{Input.}
An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
public statement of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Repair.}
A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.

\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
obligation.

\section{The main failure mode}

Suppose the paper proves
\[
  H \Longrightarrow C.
\]
During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
paper theorem should be represented as
\[
  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
\]
where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
public statement is a different theorem:
\[
  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
\]
It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
conclusion.

This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
named internal proof obligation.

\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}

Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
condition used implicitly in the paper.

The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.

\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}

Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
the wrong definition is still upstream.

When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
protocol.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
  relating the existing definition to the source object.
  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
\end{enumerate}

This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.

\section{Allowed shapes}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
\hline
Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
proof-obligation hypotheses \\
Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
proof-complete for that theorem \\
Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
source theorem instead of being produced \\
Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved
fields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\
Paper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &
Justifies silent statement drift without a repair plan
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}

When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in
  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
  first missing intermediate assertion.
  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
  paper-gap discrepancy.
  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
  hypothesis.
  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
  it.
  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation
  notes, not in the source theorem block.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Retirement criterion}

An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the
following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
        outside result;
  \item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;
  \item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,
        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper
        proof requires.
\end{enumerate}
If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it
should remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.
It should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should
not support a source-labelled blueprint \verb|\leanok| claim.

\section{Review questions}

A reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited
source statement, checking both hypotheses and conclusion up to faithful formal
encoding.  Bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, and
proof-obligation assumptions should be absent from paper-facing theorem
signatures unless they occur in the paper.  If a conditional helper remains,
its name should be explicitly conditional and it should not support a source
theorem \verb|\leanok| claim.
Each load-bearing obligation-structure or input field should have a theorem
discharging it, a tracked issue, or an explicit \verb|sorry| at the obligation
site.  When a definition has changed, the downstream subtree should be checked
against the corrected definition rather than patched locally.  Finally, if the
formal statement genuinely differs from the source statement, a paper-gap note
should explain the mathematical difference and give a plan to remove or justify
it.

named internal obligation needed by its proof, is less misleading than a source

     3	/-!
     4	# Unrestricted point errors in the extended-line obligation
     5	
     6	Every projective joint point family satisfies the fields of `CombinedPointsWitness`
     7	at some finite error. A quadratic deterministic answer, however, has small agreement
     8	with every linear coefficient answer. These facts support the obstruction to the
     9	unrestricted supplied-point domain; they do not construct extended-line witnesses.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:993-1034`.
    14	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex`, the extended-line
    15	  supplied-point obstruction, tracked by issue #509.
    16	- The coefficient collision estimate is reused from
    17	  `directCoefficientCollision_avg_le`.

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	/-- An unrestricted scalar error admits every projective joint point family.
    27	The finitely many placement comparisons have a common real upper bound. This is
    28	a Lean-only observation about the witness domain, not the point construction of
    29	`lem:qld-4-10`: no dependence of the bound on the strategy error is asserted. -/
    30	theorem CombinedPointsWitness.exists_error_of_projective
    31	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    32	    (Q : (side : PlayerSide) → (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) →
    33	      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) →
    34	      Quantum.Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side))
    35	    (hQ : ∀ side x z, Measurement.IsProjective (Q side x z)) :
    36	    ∃ δ : ℝ, ∃ points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ, points.Q = Q := by
    37	  let law := uniformDistribution
    38	    ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    39	  let selfError (p : Placement × Placement) := opFamilyDistSq law
    40	    (fun xz ab => S.place p.1 ((Q p.1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    41	    (fun xz ab => S.place p.2 ((Q p.2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab)) S.psiHat
    42	  let xzError (p : Placement × Placement) := opFamilyDistSq law
    43	    (fun xz ab => S.place p.1 ((Q p.1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    44	    (fun xz ab => S.place p.2
    45	      ((S.pointMeasExp p.2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
    46	        (S.pointMeasExp p.2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2)) S.psiHat
    47	  let zxError (p : Placement × Placement) := opFamilyDistSq law
    48	    (fun xz ab => S.place p.1 ((Q p.1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    49	    (fun xz ab => S.place p.2
    50	      ((S.pointMeasExp p.2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    51	        (S.pointMeasExp p.2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)) S.psiHat
    52	  obtain ⟨δ, hδ⟩ := Finite.bddAbove_range
    53	    (fun p => max (selfError p) (max (xzError p) (zxError p)))
    54	  have hbound (p : Placement × Placement) := hδ (Set.mem_range_self p)
    55	  refine ⟨δ, ⟨Q, hQ, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, rfl⟩
    56	  · intro p1 p2 _
    57	    exact (le_max_left _ _).trans (hbound (p1, p2))
    58	  · intro p1 p2 _
    59	    exact ((le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)).trans (hbound (p1, p2))
    60	  · intro p1 p2 _
    61	    exact ((le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)).trans (hbound (p1, p2))
    62	
    63	/-- A coefficient answer with zero quadratic coefficient agrees with a nonzero
    64	multiple of the square function on at most a `2 / q` fraction of the field.
    65	This is the Lean-only scalar part of the X-axis obstruction for `m = d = 1` in issue #509;
    66	the existing coefficient collision theorem supplies the root count. -/
    67	theorem linear_quadratic_agreement_le (D : DirectLdParams)
    68	    (f : DirectDegPoly D 2) (hf : f 2 = 0)
    69	    (α : DirectScalarQ D) (hα : α ≠ 0) :
    70	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ D))
    71	      (fun t => if evalCoefficient f t = α * t ^ 2 then (1 : ℝ) else 0) ≤
    72	      2 / (D.q : ℝ) := by
    73	  classical
    74	  let quadratic : DirectDegPoly D 2 := fun i => if i = 2 then α else 0
    75	  have hne : f ≠ quadratic := by
    76	    intro heq
    77	    have hcoeff := congrFun heq 2
    78	    simp only [quadratic, ite_true, hf] at hcoeff
    79	    exact hα hcoeff.symm
    80	  have heval (t : DirectScalarQ D) : evalCoefficient quadratic t = α * t ^ 2 := by
    81	    simp [evalCoefficient, quadratic, ite_mul]
    82	  simpa only [heval, Nat.cast_ofNat] using directCoefficientCollision_avg_le D 2 f quadratic hne
    83	
    84	end

   186	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1)

   188	      fun sample => ((sample.1.1, sample.2), sample.1.2)

   191	noncomputable def subLineZComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   192	    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
   193	    Distribution
   194	      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   195	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   196	  (Distribution.prod
   197	    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1).map Prod.fst)
   198	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2)).map
   199	      fun sample => ((sample.1, sample.2.1), sample.2.2)
   200

   202	paper lines 1063--1069.  Its extended-line marginal is the directly indexed
   203	line-point law rather than the seed-indexed line-point distribution over
   204	`F_q^(2m+2)` of the source statement; that replacement is documented in
   205	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, so this is a
   206	formalization auxiliary record, not the source-labelled statement.  Its
   207	source-mixture field records the X and Z point marginals separately; it does
   208	not assert a joint conditional law for the pair of projected points. -/

   213	  isProbability : D.IsProbability
   214	  /-- Its extended-line marginal is the direct line-point marginal. -/
   215	  extended_marginal : D.map Prod.fst =
   216	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst
   217	  /-- Every point of an extended line projects onto both stored source lines. -/
   218	  incidence : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, ∀ u ∈ sample.1.pointSet,
   219	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.1.pointSet ∧
   220	      projZ (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.2.pointSet
   221	  /-- Each line triple carries affine data sufficient for
   222	  `combineLinePoly_spec`. -/
   223	  compatibility : ∀ sample ∈ D.support,
   224	    ∃ aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta : PauliScalar P,
   225	      IsCombineLineCompatible
   226	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.base)
   227	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.direction)
   228	        sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction
   229	        sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
   230	        aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta
   231	  /-- Each one-point projected marginal is a mixture of restricted product
   232	  laws.  No equality for their joint conditional law is claimed. -/
   233	  source_mixture : ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P),
   234	    components.IsProbability ∧
   235	      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineXProjection =
   236	        Distribution.bind components (subLineXComponentDist P) ∧
   237	      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineZProjection =
   238	        Distribution.bind components (subLineZComponentDist P)
   239	  /-- An extended axis line has axis-parallel projected lines. -/
   240	  axis_closure : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, sample.1.kind = .axis ->
   241	    sample.2.1.kind = .axis ∧ sample.2.2.kind = .axis
   242	
   243	/-! ## Extended lines and global polynomial pairs -/
   244	
   245	/-- Extended-line POVMs and directly indexed, completed-answer forms of the two
   246	consistency relations in `lem:qld-4-13`, paper lines 1020--1034. The direct line
   247	carrier avoids the dimension-divisibility obstruction documented in
   248	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/
   249	structure ExtendedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
   250	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
   251	    (δ : ℝ) where
   252	  /-- The complete extended-line measurement on each player side. -/
   253	  Qline : (side : PlayerSide) -> DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ->
   254	    Measurement (DirectDegPoly P.extendedDirectLd (P.m * P.d + 1))
   255	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)

   259	      (Qline side line).effect f = 0

   264	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AA'
   265	      (((Qline .alice sample.1).postprocess
   266	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   267	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   268	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BA''
   269	      (((points.Q .bob
   270	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   271	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   272	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   273	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   274	    S.psiHat <= δ
   275	  /-- Bob's evaluated line measurement is consistent with Alice's completed
   276	  combined point measurement. -/
   277	  consistent_bob : consistencyDefect
   278	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd)
   279	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BB'
   280	      (((Qline .bob sample.1).postprocess
   281	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   282	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   283	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AB''
   284	      (((points.Q .alice
   285	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   286	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   287	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   288	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   289	    S.psiHat <= δ
   290	
   291	/-- The side-indexed global polynomial-pair measurements handed to Chapter 16.
   292	This is the exact conclusion of `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1267--1274, with
   293	the two heterogeneous point-consistency displays stated separately. -/
   294	structure GlobalPairWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   295	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (δ : ℝ) where

   297	  Smeas : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   298	    Measurement (PolyPair P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   299	  /-- Both global polynomial-pair measurements are projective. -/

item.text: Both Lean lemmas are structurally plausible: the first bounds the finite family of witness errors by one scalar, and the second is a direct specialization of the existing collision bound. I’m now checking the more delicate bridge in the prose, namely whether `consistencyDefect` against a deterministic point effect really reduces to the stated POVM disagreement probability with the claimed normalization.

    24	
    25	\begin{itemize}
    26	  \item \textbf{Difficulty: easy.}  No step of the retained proof route is
    27	  in doubt.  The obstruction is that the error function claimed in the
    28	  statement of the combined-lines lemma of the Pauli basis analysis,
    29	  $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is not delivered by either of the two
    30	  derivations printed in its source proof: one route establishes

    65	\section{Key theorem forms}
    66	
    67	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
    68	test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
    69	under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
    70	approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
    71	$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
    72	with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
    73	lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
    74	$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
    75	consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
    76	$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and
    77	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}} = \poly(\eps)$ is the line--point consistency
    78	error of the strategy.  The lemma under discussion asserts that a
    79	measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
    80	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
    81	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
    82	measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
    83	register-swapped counterpart.%
    84	\footnote{In the mirror of the source consulted here,
    85	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}: the
    86	lemma statement, with the error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is at
    87	lines~1020--1034 (label \path{lem:qld-4-13}); the central display with
    88	the first-route bound at lines~1134--1137
    89	(label \path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}); the three claims at
    90	lines~1140--1239 (labels \path{claim:17-1}--\path{claim:17-3}); the
    91	second-route conclusion $O(m^2\delta_P)$ at lines~1241--1245, preceded by
    92	a duplicated sentence whose second copy carries a malformed reference;
    93	the product-distribution estimate invoked there at lines~1055--1061
    94	(label \path{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}); and the sub-line lemma at
    95	lines~1063--1116 (label \path{lem:qld-sublines}).}
    96	The comparison involves four forms of the error function
    97	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.
    98	\begin{enumerate}
    99	  \item \textbf{Source form.}
   100	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = \poly(m^2\eps,\, md/q)$.  This is the form
   101	  printed in the statement.  Neither printed derivation supports it.
   102	  \item \textbf{Established form (first route).}
   103	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}
   104	  = O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   105	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)$, a function of the form
   106	  $m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$.
   107	  \item \textbf{Second-route form (conditional).}
   108	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = O(m^2 \delta_P)
   109	  = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$, conditional on a joint-law
   110	  decomposition that the sub-line lemma, as stated, does not provide.
   111	  \item \textbf{Consumer requirement.}  The unique consumer, the
   112	  polynomial-pair lemma, feeds $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$ into an error

   120	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
   121	
   122	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   123	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   124	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   125	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   126	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   127	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   128	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   129	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   130	
   131	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   132	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   133	order
   134	\[
   135	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   136	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   137	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   138	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   139	\]
   140	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   141	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   142	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   143	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   144	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   145	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   146	
   147	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   148	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   149	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   150	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   151	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   152	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   153	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   154	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   155	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   156	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   157	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   158	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   159	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   160	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   161	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   162	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   163	
   164	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   165	\[
   166	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   167	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   168	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   169	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   170	\]
   171	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   172	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   173	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   174	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.
   175	
   176	The remaining construction target is
   177	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   178	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it asks for evaluated consistency
   179	of the explicit unconditioned measurement
   180	\[
   181	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   182	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   183	\]
   184	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   185	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
   186	placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
   187	pasting argument at lines 942--961 are the intended discharge. The POVM,
   188	axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.
   189	
   190	A bound for a measurement conditioned on nondegenerate lines would not by
   191	itself discharge this target. It would also require a defined conditioning
   192	event, its probability, an estimate for the discarded contribution, and a
   193	transfer of the defect back to the unconditioned measurement above under the
   194	original product law. No such transfer is asserted here. In particular,
   195	the preserved conditioned construction is not identified with
   196	\path{combinedLineMeasurement}; its saved proof remains historical work.
   197	The current target retains its explicit unfinished proof, without assuming

   200	\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}
   201	
   202	The same quantitative omission remains in the auxiliary
   203	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
   204	function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
   205	at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does
   206	not remove this obstruction. The first-route estimate
   207	$C m g(\eps,md/q)$ in
   208	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness} has the same
   209	problem: it still tends to zero at $\eps=0$ with fixed $m,d$ and increasing $q$.
   210	These unrestricted auxiliaries are tracked by \ghissue{509} and \ghissue{511},
   211	respectively. The source instead uses the family constructed by its point lemma,
   212	with $\delta_Q=\poly(\eps)$, and defines the scalar answer by
   213	$c=\alpha a+\beta b$. Claim~17-1 explicitly retains the point error.
   214	\footnote{The source passages are \path{lem:qld-4-10}, \path{lem:qld-4-12}, and
   215	\path{claim:17-1} in
   216	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   217	lines~689--709, 993--1018, and 1140--1173.}
   218	
   219	Take $m=d=1$, $\eps=0$, and let $q=2^{2k+1}>2$ tend to infinity.
   220	These parameters are admissible. The Pauli basis test has a perfect projective strategy by
   221	\path{lem:pauli-completeness}.\footnote{See
   222	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   223	lines~1229--1421, for the construction; the statement and its projective Pauli
   224	measurements appear at lines~1232--1255.}
   225	Let $\hat\psi$ be its normalized expanded state. On each player's expanded
   226	local space, define the supplied joint point measurement by
   227	\[
   228	 Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
   229	 \begin{cases}
   230	   \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
   231	   0,&\text{otherwise}.
   232	 \end{cases}
   233	\]
   234	This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
   235	every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
   236	two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
   237	maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
   238	point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.
   239	
   240	The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
   241	indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
   242	of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
   243	On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
   244	in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
   245	parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
   246	has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
   247	two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
   248	most $2/q$.
   249	
   250	This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
   251	be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
   252	player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and
   253	$\sum_p w_p=1$; the axis-degree field makes $w_p=0$ for higher-degree answers.
   254	The opposite point effect is deterministically the identity at $\alpha x^2$,
   255	so the agreement is precisely the $w_p$-weighted average of those root-count
   256	fractions. These weights depend on the line but not on $x$ along it. Averaging
   257	over the fixed coordinates, and using nonnegativity of the defect on the
   258	remaining question branches, gives for either player orientation
   259	\[
   260	 \operatorname{defect}\ \ge\
   261	 \frac18\left(1-\frac1q\right)\left(1-\frac2q\right).
   262	\]
   263	There is no undefined evaluation on these nonzero axis directions, so the
   264	completed answer alphabet does not change this calculation. The scalar field
   265	identification preserves the polynomial evaluations and their root counts.
   266	
   267	The lower bound tends to $1/8$. In contrast, the predicate
   268	\path{IsPolyErr}\textsubscript{2} bounds the proposed error at these parameters by
   269	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(0,1/q)\le Cq^{-s}$ with $s>0$, which tends to zero.
   270	For the first-route estimate, the polynomial-error bound on $g$ likewise gives
   271	fixed constants $K\ge1$ and $r,s>0$ with
   272	$C g(0,1/q)\le CKq^{-s}\longrightarrow0$.
   273	Consequently both unrestricted supplied-point auxiliaries are false,
   274	independently of the printed-error discrepancy and the diagonal-line degeneracy.
   275	This argument does not refute the existential point-witness declarations or the source
   276	\path{lem:qld-4-13}; neither requires a line approximation to every arbitrarily
   277	chosen point family.
   278	
   279	Two parts of the obstruction are independently verified in Lean: every
   280	projective joint family admits some finite witness error, and a coefficient
   281	answer with zero quadratic coefficient agrees with a nonzero multiple of the
   282	square function with probability at most $2/q$.\footnote{The declarations are
   283	\path{CombinedPointsWitness.exists_error_of_projective} and
   284	\path{linear_quadratic_agreement_le} in
   285	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/PointErrorObstruction.lean}. The first uses the
   286	existence of an upper bound for a finite set of real numbers; the second reuses
   287	\path{directCoefficientCollision_avg_le}, which reduces to Mathlib's

   289	mathematical argument above, not a Lean counterexample theorem: the formal
   290	perfect-strategy construction and the formal integration of the lower bound
   291	remain to be supplied.}
   292	The existing auxiliary signatures and their unfinished proofs are preserved

   299	\section{The source assertion and the two routes}
   300	
   301	The source proof in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} constructs $\hat Q^{\ell}_f$ by
   302	averaging, over a distribution $D$ on tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$
   303	provided by its sub-line lemma, the pushforward of
   304	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ along a combining map, and reduces the lemma to a
   305	bound on the scalar consistency defect
   306	\begin{equation}
   307	  \Lambda \,=\,
   308	  \E_{(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z) \sim D}\
   309	  \E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta) \in \ell}
   310	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   311	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   312	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   313	  \ket{\hat\psi}\,,
   314	  \tag{\path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}}
   315	\end{equation}
   316	in which the point $(x,z,\alpha,\beta)$ is uniform on $\ell$ and the sum
   317	ranges over pairs of line polynomials.  The proof then bounds $\Lambda$
   318	twice, by different routes and with different results, and the printed
   319	record is internally inconsistent: the display introducing $\Lambda$
   320	asserts the first-route bound, while the closing lines assert the
   321	second-route bound as the operative one; the lemma statement claims a
   322	third form matching neither.
   323	
   324	\paragraph{The first route.}
   325	Three claims are chained.  The combined point measurement
   326	$\hat Q^{x,z}$ is replaced by the ordered product of the two point
   327	measurements at cost $\delta_Q^{1/2}$; the $X$-point factor is removed at
   328	cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$; and the remaining $Z$-point
   329	correlation is shown to be within
   330	$\sqrt{m}\,(\delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} + \eps^{1/4})$ of one.  The
   331	factors of $m$ enter through the mixture structure of the sub-line
   332	distribution: each restricted line distribution carries mixture weight
   333	$1/(2m)$ in the line-point distribution, so an average bounded by
   334	$\delta$ over the full distribution is bounded only by $2m\delta$ over a
   335	restricted component and by $4m^2\delta$ over a product of two
   336	components, and the Cauchy--Schwarz steps halve the exponents.  Chaining
   337	the claims gives
   338	\begin{equation*}
   339	  \Lambda \,=\, O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   340	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)
   341	  \,=\, m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)\,.
   342	\end{equation*}
   343	One intermediate assertion needs a harmless correction: the final line
   344	of the proof of the second claim asserts the bound
   345	$O(m^2 \delta_{\mathrm{Line}})$ for a consistency term that is close to
   346	one, rather than for its deficit.  Read as a bound on the deficit ---
   347	which is what the surrounding Cauchy--Schwarz argument requires and what
   348	the invoked line--point consistency provides after the mixture
   349	inflation --- the claim and its use are correct, with the square root of
   350	the deficit giving the stated cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$.
   351	
   352	\paragraph{The second route.}
   353	After the chain, the source restarts: it asserts that, by Property~2 of
   354	its sub-line lemma, $\Lambda$ is a mixture, over types
   355	$\mathrm{v}_1, \mathrm{v}_2 \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and
   356	indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$, of terms
   357	\begin{equation*}
   358	  \E_{(\ell_X, x) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_1,i}}\
   359	  \E_{(\ell_Z, z) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_2,j}}
   360	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   361	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   362	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   363	  \ket{\hat\psi}
   364	\end{equation*}
   365	over two \emph{independently} sampled restricted line-point pairs,
   366	bounds each term by $O(m^2\delta_P)$ using the restricted-distribution
   367	consequence of the two-basis line lemma, and concludes
   368	$\Lambda = O(m^2\delta_P)$.  The invoked decomposition concerns the
   369	\emph{joint} law of the pair $((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z))$, where $x$ and
   370	$z$ are the two blocks of the single point sampled on $\ell$.  Property~2
   371	of the sub-line lemma does not assert this joint law: it asserts the
   372	component-wise product law of the pair of \emph{lines}
   373	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, and the conditional uniformity of each point on its
   374	line separately --- equivalently, the laws of the two pairs
   375	$((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z'))$ and $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, z))$ in which
   376	the \emph{other} point is resampled independently.  These marginal
   377	statements are exactly what the first route's claims consume, each
   378	involving one point at a time; the joint decomposition used by the
   379	second route is a strictly stronger property and is not established by
   380	the lemma it is attributed to.

   382	\section{Why neither route yields the stated form}
   383	
   384	The stated error form is $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, a function of the two
   385	quantities $m^2\eps$ and $md/q$ that vanishes as both vanish.  The
   386	first-route bound is not dominated by any such function: along the
   387	scaling $\eps = m^{-4}$ with $q/(md) \to \infty$, both $m^2\eps = m^{-2}$
   388	and $md/q$ tend to $0$, while the term $m\,\eps^{1/4} = 1$ does not.
   389	Hence the established derivation supports no bound of the claimed form.
   390	This obstruction persists on the admissible numerical domain, even if the
   391	first-route term is capped by the independent unit bound on consistency.
   392	Indeed, set $m_n=2^{2n+1}$, $d_n=1$, $q_n=m_n^3$, and
   393	$\eps_n=m_n^{-4}$. The field-size exponent $6n+3$ is odd and
   394	$m_n\mid q_n$, so these parameters are admissible. Both $m_n^2\eps_n$
   395	and $m_nd_n/q_n$ equal $m_n^{-2}$ and tend to zero, whereas
   396	$\min\{1,m_n\eps_n^{1/4}\}=1$. Thus no bound of the corrected sum form
   397	$C((m^2\eps)^r+(md/q)^s)$ with positive exponents can dominate this
   398	capped term uniformly.%
   399	\footnote{This numerical obstruction is proved by
   400	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.not\_exists\_combining\_quarter\_power\_bound} in
   401	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ErrorObstruction.lean}, tracked by
   402	\ghissue{510}. It does not construct a strategy attaining the first-route
   403	upper bound and does not refute the extended-line existence statement.}
   404	The second-route bound, even granting the missing decomposition, carries
   405	the separate prefactor $m^2$: writing $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$
   406	with some fixed positive exponents, the contribution
   407	$m^2 (md/q)^{c}$ is not dominated by any vanishing function of $m^2\eps$
   408	and $md/q$, as the scaling $\eps = 0$, $md/q = m^{-2/c}$ shows, and the
   409	$\eps$-contribution fails similarly for sublinear exponents.  Neither
   410	observation asserts that the \emph{conclusion} of the lemma is false for
   411	some error function of the claimed form; the defect is that the printed
   412	proof does not deliver it.
   413	
   414	For orientation, the algebraic identity
   415	$m\,\eps^{1/2} = (m^2\eps)^{1/2}$ shows what a derivation of the claimed
   416	$\eps$-dependence would need: a chain that loses only square roots in the
   417	$\eps$-type quantities \emph{after} the restricted-distribution
   418	inflation would produce terms of the shape $(m^2\eps)^{1/2}$.  The
   419	printed chain loses fourth roots, through two nested Cauchy--Schwarz
   420	steps applied to already square-rooted quantities, and its
   421	$md/q$-dependence enters as $m\,\delta_P^{1/4}$, which the claimed form
   422	cannot absorb.

   517	
   518	There is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma, together with an
   519	intermediate inconsistency: the printed proof asserts two different

   521	$O(m(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} +

   683	In this section our goal is to create a set of combined measurements

   689	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:qld-4-10}

   691		For every $x,z \in \F_q^m$ and $\mH \in \{ \mH_\alice, \mH_\bob\}$ there are projective measurements $\{ \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} \}_{a,b \in \F_q}$ acting on $\mathcal{H} \otimes (\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ such that:
   692		\begin{enumerate}
   693			\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random $x,z \in \F_q^m$,
   694			\begin{equation}
   695				\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}
   696				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\alice \alice'}  \approx_{\delta_Q} (\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\bob \alice''}\,.
   697			\end{equation}

   699			\item (\textbf{Consistency with $\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly random $x,z \in \F_q^m$,
   700			\begin{gather}
   701				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}
   702					(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_Q} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,X),x}_{a} \hat{M}^{(\Point,Z),z}_b)_{\bob \alice''}\;, \\
   703								\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}
   704					(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_Q} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,Z),z}_b  \hat{M}^{(\Point,X),x}_{a} )_{\bob \alice''}\;.

   168	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary for items 1–5 and 7 of `lem:qld-win-implications`:

   170	of source outcomes whose postprocessed labels differ. -/
   171	theorem consistencyDefect_postprocess_eq_mismatch
   172	    {G : Game} {X β : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
   173	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   174	    (μ : Distribution X) (S : Strategy G)
   175	    (qA : X → G.QuestionA) (qB : X → G.QuestionB)
   176	    (fA : X → G.AnswerA → β) (fB : X → G.AnswerB → β) :
   177	    consistencyDefect μ
   178	        (fun x c => heteroKron (((S.A (qA x)).postprocess (fA x)).effect c) 1)
   179	        (fun x c => heteroKron 1 (((S.B (qB x)).postprocess (fB x)).effect c))
   180	        S.ψ =
   181	      avgOver μ (fun x => outcomeEventWeight S (qA x) (qB x)
   182	        (fun a b => fA x a ≠ fB x b)) := by
   183	  unfold consistencyDefect outcomeEventWeight

   188	  simp_rw [DistanceCalculus.placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   189	  have hmass (c d : β) :
   190	      DistanceCalculus.stateQForm S.ψ
   191	          (heteroKron
   192	            (∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => fA x a = c),

   191	/-! ## The abstract one-point deficit -/
   192	
   193	/-- Let `A` be a complete measurement, `Q` a projective measurement, `R` a
   194	family of projections and `W` a family of operators, all indexed by the same
   195	outcomes, with `Q`, `R` and `W` commuting with the effects of `A` and with
   196	`W R = W`.  If `A` and `Q` are consistent with defect at most `η` and `Q` is
   197	within squared distance `ζ` of `Wᴴ`, then the deficit of the overlap of `A`
   198	with `R` is at most `2 √η + 2 √ζ`.  The proof inserts `Q` before `R`, replaces
   199	`Q R` by `W R = W`, and compares `W` with `Q`; each of the three steps is a
   200	Cauchy--Schwarz estimate weighted by `A`.  This is the common estimate behind
   201	the deficits in the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, paper
   202	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1239`. -/
   203	theorem one_sub_overlap_le_of_consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
   204	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   205	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   206	    (μ : Distribution X) (A Q : X → Measurement α ι) (R W : X → α → Op ι)
   207	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
   208	    (hQ : ∀ x, Measurement.IsProjective (Q x)) (hR : ∀ x a, IsProj (R x a))
   209	    (hAQ : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((Q x).effect a))
   210	    (hAR : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (R x a))
   211	    (hAW : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (W x a))
   212	    (hWR : ∀ x a, W x a * R x a = W x a)
   213	    (hnonneg : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a))
   214	    (η ζ : ℝ)
   215	    (hcons : consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => (A x).effect a)
   216	      (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ ≤ η)
   217	    (hdist : opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => (Q x).effect a)
   218	      (fun x a => (W x a)ᴴ) ψ ≤ ζ) :
   219	    1 - avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * R x a)) ≤
   220	      2 * Real.sqrt η + 2 * Real.sqrt ζ := by
   221	  set ovQ := avgOver μ (fun x =>
   222	    ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (Q x).effect a)) with hovQ
   223	  have h1 : 1 - ovQ ≤ η := by
   224	    rw [← consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap μ A Q ψ hμ hψ]
   225	    exact hcons
   226	  have hovQ_nonneg : 0 ≤ ovQ :=
   227	    avgOver_nonneg μ _ fun x => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => hnonneg x a
   228	  have hovQ_le : ovQ ≤ 1 :=
   229	    avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one μ A (fun x a => (Q x).effect a) ψ hμ hψ
   230	      (fun x a => hQ x a) hAQ
   231	  have h1' : 1 - ovQ ≤ Real.sqrt η := by
   232	    have h0 : 0 ≤ 1 - ovQ := by linarith
   233	    calc 1 - ovQ = Real.sqrt ((1 - ovQ) ^ 2) := (Real.sqrt_sq h0).symm
   234	      _ ≤ Real.sqrt η := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (by nlinarith)
   235	  -- comparing `Q` with `W` under the weight `A`
   236	  have hWconj : ∀ x a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a) =
   237	      stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (W x a)ᴴ) := by
   238	    intro x a
   239	    rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose ψ ((A x).effect a * W x a),
   240	      Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, measurement_effect_hermitian]

    25	/-- Two distinct direct coefficient vectors of degree at most `degree` agree
    26	at a uniformly sampled parameter with probability at most `degree / q`.

    29	answer format and apply Schwartz-Zippel to a later multivariate collision term;
    30	they do not state this exact univariate averaging bound.
    31	
    32	The estimate has no hypothesis `degree < q`; when the displayed bound exceeds
    33	one it remains a valid, deliberately nontruncated root-count bound. -/

    36	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ D))
    37	        (fun t => if evalCoefficient a t = evalCoefficient b t then
    38	          (1 : ℝ) else 0) ≤
    39	      (degree : ℝ) / (D.q : ℝ) := by

    41	  let collisionSet : Finset (DirectScalarQ D) :=
    42	    Finset.univ.filter fun t => evalCoefficient a t = evalCoefficient b t
    43	  have hcollision_card : collisionSet.card ≤ degree :=
    44	    evalCoefficient_collision_card_le a b hne
    45	  calc
    46	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ D))
    47	        (fun t => if evalCoefficient a t = evalCoefficient b t then
    48	          (1 : ℝ) else 0) =
    49	        (collisionSet.card : ℝ) /
    50	          Fintype.card (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    51	      calc

    53	            (fun t => if evalCoefficient a t = evalCoefficient b t then
    54	              (1 : ℝ) else 0) =

    56	              if evalCoefficient a t = evalCoefficient b t then

    33	actual polynomial composition operation. -/
    34	noncomputable def linePolynomialOfCoefficients {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    35	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
    36	  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val
    37	
    38	/-- Evaluating the polynomial represented by a coefficient list agrees with
    39	`evalCoefficient`. -/
    40	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    41	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) (t : K) :
    42	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).eval t = evalCoefficient f t := by
    43	  change Polynomial.eval t
    44	      (∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val) =
    45	    ∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, f i * t ^ i.val
    46	  rw [Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
    47	  simp
    48	
    49	/-- The coefficient polynomial agrees with Mathlib's coefficient-vector
    50	construction. -/
    51	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    52	    [DecidableEq K] {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) :
    53	    linePolynomialOfCoefficients f = Polynomial.ofFn (c + 1) f := by
    54	  simp only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients, Polynomial.ofFn_eq_sum_monomial,
    55	    Polynomial.C_mul_X_pow_eq_monomial]
    56	
    57	/-- Distinct bounded coefficient vectors represent distinct polynomials. -/
    58	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_injective {K : Type*} [Semiring K] (c : ℕ) :
    59	    Function.Injective (linePolynomialOfCoefficients (K := K) (c := c)) := by
    60	  classical
    61	  intro first second heq
    62	  exact Polynomial.injective_ofFn (c + 1)
    63	    (by simpa only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn] using heq)
    64	
    65	/-- The polynomial of a bounded coefficient vector has degree at most `n`. -/
    66	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
    67	    (f : Fin (n + 1) → K) :
    68	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).natDegree ≤ n := by
    69	  classical
    70	  rw [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn]
    71	  exact Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Polynomial.ofFn_natDegree_lt (Nat.succ_pos n) f)
    72	
    73	/-- Distinct coefficient polynomials of degree at most `bound` agree at no
    74	more than `bound` elements of a finite integral domain. This is the univariate
    75	root bound underlying the Schwartz-Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:955`.
    77	No restriction of the degree relative to the field size is required. -/
    78	theorem evalCoefficient_collision_card_le {K : Type*} [CommRing K] [IsDomain K]
    79	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {bound : ℕ}
    80	    (first second : Fin (bound + 1) → K) (hne : first ≠ second) :
    81	    (Finset.univ.filter fun param => evalCoefficient first param =
    82	      evalCoefficient second param).card ≤ bound := by
    83	  classical
    84	  by_contra hcard
    85	  have heq := Polynomial.eq_of_natDegree_lt_card_of_eval_eq'
    86	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients first) (linePolynomialOfCoefficients second)
    87	    (Finset.univ.filter fun param => evalCoefficient first param =
    88	      evalCoefficient second param)
    89	    (fun param hparam => by
    90	      simpa only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval] using (Finset.mem_filter.mp hparam).2)
    91	    (lt_of_le_of_lt (max_le (linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le first)
    92	      (linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le second)) (Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcard))
    93	  exact hne (linePolynomialOfCoefficients_injective bound heq)
    94	
    95	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

Against the deterministic identity/zero point measurement, that diagonal overlap is exactly the line POVM’s Born weight on agreeing evaluations. I’m checking the remaining quantitative details: admissibility of the parameter family, the exact direct-line sampling law, and whether the “perfect strategy” cited by the note supplies the formal setting it invokes.

     5	# Pauli basis test soundness interface
     6	
     7	This module contains the quantitative error function and the closed definitions
     8	used to state Pauli basis test soundness.  The carriers are concrete
     9	finite-dimensional vectors and matrices so that the soundness proof can use the
    10	existing Hilbert-space API without introducing a dependency cycle.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The interface supports blueprint
    15	`thm:pauli`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The distance functionals use blueprint `def:state-distance` and
    18	`def:povm-distance`.
    19	-/

    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

    24

    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
